text:
### Observed differences

- The frequencies of two alternative activity blocks swapped almost exactly. In the earlier window, A24, A25 and A26 each took part in about 82 in 100 traces and the three ran together in 82 in 100, while A21, A22 and A23 each took part in only about 20 in 100 (appearing together when they appeared at all). In the later window, A21, A22 and A23 each take part in about 79–80 in 100 traces (together in about 79), while A24, A25 and A26 each appear in only about 21–22 in 100 (together in about 21). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, REL017, REL025, REL038, REL043]

- The split manifests in A20's outgoing transitions: before, about 82 in 100 of them led to A24/A25/A26 and about 18 in 100 to A21/A22/A23; in the later window, about 78 in 100 lead to A21/A22/A23 and about 21 in 100 to A24/A25/A26. A20 precedes A21/A22/A23 in about 77–78 in 100 traces (before about 18–19) and precedes A24/A25/A26 in about 21 in 100 (before about 80–82). [DIR005, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]

- The shared downstream tail keeps its members but is re-attached: A21/A22/A23 now precede A30, A34 and A35 in about 77–79 in 100 traces (before about 19–20), whereas A24/A25/A26 previously preceded A34/A35 in about 80 in 100 and now do so in about 21. A34 itself still occurs in every trace in both windows. [REL022, REL023, REL024, REL029, REL030, REL035, REL036, REL041, REL045, REL048, POS003]

- A34 now leads almost always straight to A35: about 90 in 100 of its outgoing transitions go to A35 (before about 56) and only about 2 in 100 to A06 (before about 45); the A34→A35 pair is immediately consecutive in about 92 in 100 cases (before about 56). [DIR006, LAG006]

- A06 receded and changed placement: participation fell from about 46 to about 12 in 100 traces, its mean event position moved from about 0.91 to about 0.52 of the trace, and its outgoing transitions are no longer dominated by A35 (about 92 in 100 before, about 15 after, the latter from only some 26 observed transitions). [OCC003, POS001, DIR001, REL009, REL010]

- Smaller shifts: A02 participation rose from about 8 to about 17 in 100 traces and A04 from about 5 to about 19 (16→33 and 10→37 traces); A14→A15 (about 96 vs 87 in 100) and A19→A20 (about 97 vs 93) are essentially stable. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR003, DIR004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the choice between two existing alternative paths after A20 flipped in how often each is taken: the path through A21, A22 and A23, which then runs into the shared tail A30/A34/A35, was taken in about 19 in 100 traces before and about 79 in 100 in the later window, while the path through A24, A25 and A26 fell from about 81 to about 21 in 100. [DIR005, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009]

This is shown directly by the shift in A20's outgoing shares, with about 200 transitions behind each profile, and consistently mirrored by the participation counts (38–163 traces per side) and the changed relations of both blocks with A20 and with the tail; the internal order within each block is unchanged (mixed order in both windows), and every involved activity remains well observed in both windows (roughly 20% vs 80% participation), so this fits a shift in how often existing paths are taken rather than activities being added, removed or reordered. Each difference is larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, and with 73 qualifying items against roughly 1 expected by chance among 180 tested units, the pattern as a whole is far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces — though the many items largely describe one underlying difference, not independent confirmations. [DIR005, OCC004, OCC007, REL011, REL014, REL017, REL022, REL041]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the two windows contain different mixes of case types (for example one variant dominating the later window) rather than a changed routing decision within comparable cases. [DIR005, OCC004]

Other differences: A06 changed beyond the branch swap — in the earlier window it was a late-trace activity placed between A34 and A35 (A34 led to A06 in about 45 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, and A06 led immediately to A35 in about 98 in 100 of observed pairs), while in the later window it is rare (about 12 in 100 traces), appears early (mean position about 0.52), and A34 leads almost always straight to A35; this fits A06 being bypassed or made optional rather than a mere frequency shift. [OCC003, POS001, DIR006, LAG001, LAG006, REL009] A02 and A04 became modestly more frequent, and the distance items around A06 in the later window rest on very few observations (1–7 pairs), adding little weight. [OCC001, OCC002, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
